keyQuestions: How do Ponytail's hooks activate, persist mode, track sessions, and gate behavior per runtime, and which of those mechanisms are missing from sk-code's hooks?

graphEvents.label: Ponytail hooks vs sk-code hook layer
Single dispatch table beats per-host branching

label: Ponytail's SessionStart hook appends a budgeted codebase map (one line per folder of exported names, shared folders first, fail-open) whose stated purpose is to make reuse-first cost no search; sk-code's hook layer has no equivalent and its post-edit router only runs defect checkers. Classification: NEW - the enabler for the missing reuse rung.

Ponytail injects its ruleset into subagents through a fail-open SubagentStart hook because SessionStart context never reaches them; sk-code's task-dispatch guard evaluates dispatches but injects no active surface/mode doctrine into the spawned agent. Classification: NEW (candidate, bounded by existing guard layer; adapter cost is real).

sk-code's one path-dispatch table shared by every runtime adapter (priority-ordered, at most one checker per edit, checker code staying in owning skills) is stronger than Ponytail's per-host env detection and per-host output branching. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED (stronger).

Ponytail swallows hook failures at every step; sk-code states fail-open as a written router contract (every failure path resolves to no finding; the edit is never blocked) and the same property in session-lifecycle. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED (codified, not merely defensive).

Ponytail's per-project mode-flag machinery (SHA-256 project key plus shared fallback flag, with a documented same-repo concurrency limit) should not be ported: no sk-code consumer exists for a latched session intensity, the prior refinement rejected the intensity state machine, and sk-code keeps per-session state only where a named consumer exists. Classification: REJECT (reasoned).

Ponytail refuses to latch /ponytail-review as a session level; sk-code likewise has no session latch for review - it routes sk-code-review as a workflow mode and scopes depth to an env alias that names an existing tier. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED by design.

Ponytail treats host-quirk regression classes as product surface (stdin stall, BOM, unrecognized host, regex timeout) across four hook test suites; sk-code has hook tests and adapter suites, but whether every one of those failure classes is covered is unverified - a deliberate phase-2 test-audit item, not a claimed gap. Classification: NEW (test-class checklist).

Env-over-config-over-default precedence (PONYTAIL_DEFAULT_MODE / config.json, persisted default separate from the session switch) is already the repo idiom in sk-code-review's SK_CODE_REVIEW_DEPTH alias. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED.
